questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, what may happen?

options.text: The trailer may lean during turns.
The trailer may have extra support during turns.
The trailer may be easier to steer during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may lean during turns.
questions.explanation: When weight is on one side of a trailer, the trailer leans to that side. This increases the risk of a rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: How can you check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if an older vehicle has ABS, look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
It prevents a truck from being stolen.
It prevents the driver from driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, how should you keep it from moving?

options.text: Park it against a wall or another vehicle.
Park it on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, use wheel chocks to prevent it from moving.

questions.question: Before a trip, how can you make sure air reaches all trailers?

options.text: Check for moving air inside each trailer.
Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feel for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, wait for air pressure to build. Then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: If color-coded, which color identifies emergency or supply lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines. This helps drivers avoid mistakes when connecting glad hands.

questions.question: If color-coded, which color identifies service lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines. This helps drivers avoid mistakes when connecting glad hands.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: Compared to empty rigs, fully-loaded rigs are:

options.text: Just as likely to roll over.

questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs are more likely to roll over than empty rigs because the cargo weight gives them a higher center of gravity.

questions.question: After completing a pre-trip inspection, you should make sure that the:
questions.explanation: Before driving, open both the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves. Listen for air escaping to make sure air reaches all brakes on all trailers. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: Trailers built before ____ do not have to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When you park a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to stop it from rolling.

questions.question: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels:

options.text: Follow the same path as the front wheels.
Follow a different path than the front wheels.
Should not be a concern to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow a different path than the front wheels.
questions.explanation: When any vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Long vehicles have more off-tracking than short vehicles.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops between:
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air from flowing.

questions.question: A driver should test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Releasing air with the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, first let the air system charge fully. Turn off the engine. Then press the brake pedal several times to release air from the system. The valve should move to its emergency position when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too quickly. To prevent rollovers, keep the vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: A tractor protection valve:

options.text: Keeps air in a brake system if there is a bad leak.
Prevents a truck from being stolen.
Prevents a trailer from being accidentally released.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in a brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When crossing traffic with a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for your vehicle.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, make sure there is a large enough gap for your vehicle to safely pass through.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brakes should be applied:

options.text: In the same way as they would be in a vehicle without ABS.
As the vehicle is placed in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same way as they would be in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake a vehicle with ABS the same way you would brake a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. This means if the air supply leaks away:

options.text: The trailer will not have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will not have brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away, there will be no brakes on the trailer and the wheels will spin freely.
